title: is anyone interested in building a, algo together? or giving advice.
author: BMS-trading
selftext:
would an AI algo synchronize with other copies of itself or other algo's on the market chop?  
  
I would like to make an algo, but I don't have any of the technical skills and would appreciate any advice or help in creating an algorithm.

would an AI algorithm be self-learning enough to improve its trading executions?  
can a algo be fail Safed partly?   
to locking segments that are not meeting required percentages, to protect the account.

is there a limit on how advanced a trading bot can be within it own code?   
I know its a little silly of a question, I'm interested in knowing if you can make an algo trade multiple pair currency.

if anyone is interested in discussing in-depth, I would appreciate the help, thank you.

comments.author: senddinu
comments.body:
I'd like to collaborate as well. Currently testing a options trading rules enginevon a paper account . Built using Claude in Python, open source database. Integrated with IBKR API, leveragin live options flow data from third party subscription service. 

Decent results in live forward testing. Very small dataset so far but looks promising.

replies.author: maxxell13
replies.body: What options flow data services are you using?

replies.author: senddinu
replies.body:
I have a combination of multiple services

Massive -> Rest API for historical options data, I use the free tier and set a program to pull 5 calls per min limit. Took me 5 hr for my back test dataset 

BBS -> Options Flow historical and daily ingestion

IBKR -> Latest News, and tech chart details

comments.author: buldingkai
comments.body: a few of these i can answer from running my own setup. i'd nail the fail-safes before anything else. hard caps on max loss, drawdown and an auto-stop matter more than the entry logic, a fresh config of mine blew up 0 for 5 recently and those limits are the only reason it stayed survivable. on self-learning, be skeptical, in my experience the model is sharp on risk math and bad at direction, it doesn't quietly grow an edge. with no coding background, start tiny and paper trade before anything real.
